provenance.instrument: Borough of Elizabethtown Zoning Ordinance (Chapter 27 Zoning, Ord. 766 of 5-16-1996, as amended), as published on eCode360
provenance.status_detail: eCode360 EL0331, Borough of Elizabethtown (Lancaster County, the only Elizabethtown borough in Pennsylvania). Chapter 27 was adopted 5-16-1996 by Ord. 766 and amended since. The ADU rules were added by Ord. 983 (11-16-2017). The latest zoning amendments seen are Ord. No. 999 (6-18-2020) and Ord. No. 1009 (4-6-2023). eCode360 shows sections without the chapter number (for example '§ 1333'). This file cites them as 27-1333, the form eCode360 uses in its links. Each district part lists its uses and figures in text. The only attachment is the table of sign requirements. New Laws: none
provenance.code_current_through_note: eCode360 Version Information: 'Includes legislation through 07-17-2025.' Uploaded 06-23-2026. New Laws: 'There are currently no known new laws for this Code.'
checks: An accessory dwelling unit is a permitted use in R-1, R-2, R-3 and MU 'in accordance with § 1333' (27-602.7, 27-702.8, 27-802.12, 27-12A02.V). 'Accessory dwelling units are not permitted within the Central Business District' (27-1333.8)

The code's ADU is 'A small dwelling unit with no more than two bedrooms that is built on the same lot as a primary dwelling unit', a one- or two-bedroom unit in the basement or attic, or 'a separate dwelling unit converted from an existing or newly constructed accessory structure or portion thereof' (27-201)
One ADU per lot. The lot owner keeps his or her principal residence in the house or the ADU. The ADU may not be sold separately (27-1333.1, 4, 5)
A detached ADU must be smaller in footprint and height than the principal building and at least 6 ft from the side and rear lot lines. An attached ADU meets the district setbacks (27-1333.2, 9)

A residential accessory building stands in the rear yard of the house, not in a required front yard, and an accessory structure in a residential zone may be at most 15 ft tall (27-1302.2(2), (5), (6))
The ADU must meet the residential rental license program and the property maintenance code, and a zoning permit and a construction code permit are needed before work starts (27-1333.3, 7, 10)
Parking for accessory dwelling units is '1 per bedroom plus 2 for the dwelling unit'. Other dwellings need 2 per dwelling unit (27-1602A(4), (17))
In R-2 and R-3 the lot area and width 'are established for each dwelling unit' (27-707.1, 27-807.1). Whether an ADU needs its own lot share is not settled
In R-2 a single-family detached dwelling may not be converted into a semidetached dwelling (27-702.2)
A use neither permitted nor prohibited may be allowed by the Zoning Hearing Board as a special exception if it is of the same general character as the district's permitted uses (27-306)
27-2008 sets the usual variance findings of the state planning code and does not bar a use variance

Floodplains (Chapter 8): in the Floodway District 'All structures are prohibited except' dams, culverts, bridges and open space (8-303.1). The Flood-Fringe District is the A District and the land between the floodway and the 500-year floodplain boundary (8-301.4). Its permitted uses must not need buildings, and 'Uses not listed as a permitted use or a special use are expressly not permitted' (8-304.1, 304.3). An existing single-family house in the Flood-Fringe District may grow by at most 50% of its ground-level area at the date of Chapter 8 (8-402.1A)

In MU 'The minimum height requirement of a building shall be 35 feet' (27-12A12). Read literally it would keep out a detached ADU, which must be lower than the house and at most 15 ft. Ask the zoning officer
A conversion apartment (R-3) keeps the building's look as a single-family dwelling, with no exterior evidence of change except as building codes require (27-1304B, J)
provenance.notes: Zoning office: Borough of Elizabethtown, Zoning Officer. Read in a browser on eCode360, one page at a time, on 2026-11-16, mostly in print view. Read: Chapter 8 (Floodplains) in full on the print page, 27-1304 (conversion apartments), Part 12A (MU) in full, 27-201 (the ADU, accessory building, apartment, conversion apartment, dwelling, dwelling unit, single-family, two-family and impervious coverage definitions), 27-306, Parts 6, 7, 8 and 9, 27-1302, 27-1333, 27-1602A, 27-2008 and the New Laws page. Not read: Parts 1, 4 (OS&C), 5 (INS), 10 (G-C), 11 (LI), 12 (G-I), 27-1301, 27-1303 and 27-1305 to 27-1332 (27-1318 on access and principal structures included), 27-1334, Parts 14, 15 and 17 to 21 (27-2008 aside). A code search for single-family detached dwellings, dwelling units, caretaker, watchman, in-law, family member, ECHO and temporary dwelling found dwelling listings only in R-1, R-2, R-3, MU and CBD. The ADU text sets no floor area cap, only two bedrooms at most for a unit in the house or the basement or attic. Chapter 22 (subdivision and land development) was not read.

term.note: 'A small dwelling unit with no more than two bedrooms that is built on the same lot as a primary dwelling unit, a separate one- or two-bedroom dwelling unit in the basement, a separate one- or two-bedroom dwelling unit in the attic, or a separate dwelling unit converted from an existing or newly constructed accessory structure or portion thereof.'

status.note: A permitted use in R-1, R-2, R-3 and MU, under 27-1333. A zoning permit and a construction code permit (27-1333.10)

status_outside.note: OS&C, INS, G-C, LI and G-I do not list the ADU, and no dwelling listing was found in them

value.note: 'Accessory dwelling units are not permitted within the Central Business District.' Accessory buildings there 'may not be converted into residential units' (27-907)

path.note: Permitted use. Zoning permit and construction code permit

fallback_path.note: Zoning Hearing Board. 27-2008 sets the usual findings and does not bar a use variance

value.name: Two-family detached dwelling (R-3)
value.conditions: 'Two-family detached dwellings' are a permitted use in R-3 (27-802.3). A duplex is 'A building used by two families, with one dwelling unit arranged over the other, and having two side yards' (27-201). 3,000 sq ft of lot per unit, width 55 ft at the street and 60 ft at the setback line per unit, depth 100 ft, impervious cover 50%, front 20 ft, side 8 ft, rear 25 ft (27-807, 27-808). Two parking spaces per dwelling unit (27-1602A(17))
value.note: 6,000 sq ft is 3,000 sq ft for each of the two units. A stacked two-unit house, not an accessory unit

value.name: Conversion apartments (R-3)
value.conditions: 'Conversion apartments' are a permitted use in R-3 (27-802.5). 'Any building existing at the effective date of this chapter may be converted to a dwelling for more than one family' (27-1304). Lot 4,000 sq ft, width 45 ft at the street, 50 ft at the setback line, depth 100 ft (27-807.1). No unit under 300 sq ft of habitable floor area (27-1304A). 'There is no exterior evidence of change in the building' except as building codes require, and the building keeps its street entrance, porch and look as a single-family dwelling (27-1304B, J). At most 3 bedrooms per unit, at most three dwelling units per building, at most 3 stories, and no unit in the basement or below ground (27-1304E, G, H, I). One parking space more than Part 16 asks for a unit with more than 2 bedrooms (27-1304D). Adequate street frontage under 27-1318 (27-1304F)

requires.condition: The building existed when Chapter 27 took effect (Ord. 766 of 5-16-1996)

value.note: An existing building divided into more units, not an accessory unit. Only a building that stood on 5-16-1996 qualifies

value.name: Dwelling units above a nonresidential use (CBD)
value.conditions: 'Dwelling units, provided they are located on or above the second-floor level of a nonresidential use' (27-902.1). Ground-floor dwelling units are a conditional use (27-905A). Accessory buildings 'may not be converted into residential units' (27-907). Two off-street spaces for each unit, which Borough Council may reduce by conditional use (27-911)

requires.condition: The building holds a nonresidential use and the unit is on or above the second floor

value.note: Not a unit added to a house lot. ADUs are not permitted in the CBD (27-1333.8)

land_development_second_building.note: Land development includes 'A group of two or more residential or nonresidential buildings' on a lot. A new detached ADU is a second residential building. Chapter 22 (subdivision and land development) was not read, so ask whether a plan is needed

value.condition: A detached ADU must be smaller in both building footprint and height than the principal building on the lot.

The ADU must meet the residential rental license program (Chapter 5, Part 3) and the existing structures and property maintenance code (Chapter 5, Part 1). The lot owner secures electric, water and sewer service and pays the connection and service fees.
The ADU may not be sold separately from the principal building.

In MU a house that existed when the MU rules took effect (Ord. 876 of 8-17-2006) is a permitted residential use (27-12A02.O). New construction of residential buildings is a conditional use (27-12A04.H, 27-12A06.1), so a newer house needed that approval.
In MU 'New construction of residential buildings' is a conditional use before Borough Council (27-12A04.H, 27-12A06.1). A new detached ADU building may count as one.

disputed_by.note: The MU use list permits an 'Accessory dwelling unit in accordance with § 1333' by right, and the list of new residential buildings in 27-12A06.1 does not name an ADU

value.condition: In the Floodway District 'All structures are prohibited except' dams, culverts, bridges and open space (8-303.1). In the Flood-Fringe District permitted uses must not need buildings, and 'Uses not listed as a permitted use or a special use are expressly not permitted' (8-304.1, 304.3). A dwelling unit is not listed in either district, so no form of ADU is allowed there. Part 4 lets an existing house stay and grow within limits (8-401, 8-402.1A), but an ADU is a new dwelling unit

types_allowed.note: The definition names a unit in the basement or attic and a unit converted from 'an existing or newly constructed accessory structure or portion thereof'. 27-1333.9 names units detached from and attached to the principal building

max_sqft.note: No floor area cap. The unit has 'no more than two bedrooms', and a detached unit is smaller in footprint than the principal building (27-1333.2)

setback_side_ft.note: 'Accessory dwelling units that are detached from the principal building on the lot shall have a minimum setback of six feet from the rear and side lot line.'

front_yard_barred.note: A building accessory to a residential use 'shall be located within the rear yard of the principal building'

accessory_rear_yard_only.note: 'any building or structure accessory to a residential use shall be located within the rear yard of the principal building'

height_capped_at_house.note: A detached ADU is smaller in height than the principal building

accessory_structure_max_height_ft.note: 'The maximum height of any accessory structure within a residential zone is 15 feet.'

accessory_cap_binds_adu.note: A detached ADU is a dwelling unit 'converted from an existing or newly constructed accessory structure' (27-201), and an ADU must 'comply with all other applicable provisions' (27-1333.11). So the 15 ft accessory height in a residential zone binds it, along with 'smaller in ... height than the principal building'

value.where: An accessory building along an alley stays at least 5 ft from the alley and outside the 14 ft alley right-of-way. A private garage with its entrance on an alley stays at least 10 ft from any lot line and outside that right-of-way
in MU, where accessory setbacks are those of the principal building type. The ADU section's 6 ft for a detached unit is the more specific rule, so ask which governs

owner_occupancy.note: 'The owner of the lot shall maintain his or her principal primary residence in either the principal dwelling unit on the lot or in the accessory dwelling unit.'

max_adus.note: 'No lot shall contain more than one accessory dwelling unit.'

reading.value: 27-1602A(4) asks '1 per bedroom plus 2 for the dwelling unit' for accessory dwelling units, and the house needs 2. Read as the ADU's own count, a one-bedroom ADU needs 3 more spaces, 5 in total. Read as the bedrooms added to the house's 2, it needs 1 more, 3 in total.

min_lot_sqft.note: Single-family detached dwelling. Width 60 ft at the street, 75 ft at the setback line, depth 100 ft

max_impervious_coverage.note: The section is titled 'Lot Area, Lot Width and Impervious Coverage Regulations', and impervious coverage is the share of the lot 'covered by impervious materials' (27-201). At least 25% of the front yard stays grass

principal_max_height_ft.note: 'The height of a building shall not exceed 35 feet.'

min_lot_sqft.note: Single-family detached. Width 55 ft at the street, 60 ft at the setback line, depth 100 ft. Semidetached 4,000 sq ft per unit

max_impervious_coverage.note: The section is titled 'Lot Area, Lot Width and Impervious Coverage Regulations', and impervious coverage is the share of the lot 'covered by impervious materials' (27-201). At least 25% of the front yard stays grass

principal_max_height_ft.note: 'The height of a building shall not exceed 35 feet.'

lot_area_per_unit_sqft.note: 'The minimum lot area, lot width and lot depth requirements are established for each dwelling unit' (27-707.1). An ADU is a dwelling unit (27-201), so the lot may need 8,000 sq ft for each unit. The ADU section sets no lot area of its own

min_lot_sqft.note: Single-family detached. Width 55 ft at the street, 60 ft at the setback line, depth 100 ft

max_impervious_coverage.note: The section is titled 'Lot Area, Lot Width and Impervious Coverage Regulations', and impervious coverage is the share of the lot 'covered by impervious materials' (27-201). At least 25% of the front yard stays grass

principal_max_height_ft.note: 'The height of a building shall not exceed 35 feet.'

lot_area_per_unit_sqft.note: 'The minimum lot area, lot width and lot depth requirements are established for each dwelling unit' (27-807.1). An ADU is a dwelling unit (27-201), so the lot may need 6,000 sq ft for each unit. The ADU section sets no lot area of its own

min_lot_sqft_by_type.note: Semidetached 3,000 sq ft per unit, attached 2,500 sq ft per unit

min_lot_sqft.note: Residential uses in MU take the R-3 lot area, width and depth of 27-807 (27-12A06.3, 27-12A13.1A). A house that existed in 2006 is permitted. New residential construction is a conditional use (27-12A04.H, 27-12A06.1)

setback_side_ft.note: 'A residential use must maintain a side-yard setback of eight feet on both sides.'

max_impervious_coverage.note: New construction of residential units meets the coverage rules of 27-807.2, 50% (27-12A06.3). 27-12A15 says lot coverage 'for all uses in the district shall not exceed 65%'. The lower figure is shown
